title: Ethena's USDe outflow is rate-limited while every other instance's outflow is unlimited, because redeeming USDe is itself a counterparty interaction
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.4.1.2.4 sets the Ethena USDe instance's inflow at `maxAmount` 250,000,000 with a 100,000,000-per-day slope, and its **outflow** at `maxAmount` 500,000,000 with a 200,000,000-per-day slope. That breaks the pattern of every Centrifuge and Blackrock instance, where outflow is simply `Unlimited`.

The reason is visible in what the two "outflows" actually do. A Centrifuge outflow is a withdrawal that lands in the Grove ALM Proxy — a pure reduction in exposure, so limiting it would only impede de-risking. A USDe outflow is a **redemption through the Ethena minter**: Grove hands USDe to a counterparty and waits for USDC settled off-contract (A...2.1.2.10.4). That is a new counterparty interaction, not an exit from one, so it belongs inside the limit system.

The sUSDe instance confirms the reading: its outflow is `unlimited` in both fields (A...4.2.2.4.2), because unstaking merely moves value from the staking vault back to the proxy.

The ratio is the second design choice. Outflow capacity is exactly **double** inflow capacity on both the level and the slope, so the position can always be dismantled twice as fast as it was assembled. That asymmetry is the correct direction for any control that must not become the binding constraint during stress, and it refines the naive rule "never limit outflows" into the more accurate one: never limit *reductions in exposure*, and size the limits on exposure-creating exits generously.
description: Outflow is capped at 500,000,000 with a 200,000,000-per-day slope — exactly twice the inflow limits — whereas sUSDe unstaking, which merely returns assets to the proxy, stays unlimited.
